newsitem.title: USA: U.S. airlines cut fares to compete with American.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airlines cut fares to compete with American.

text.p: Four major U.S. airlines reduced rates on selected routes this weekend after AMR Corp's American Airlines Saturday slashed fares to win back customers scared away by the threat of pilots' strike.
Continental Airlines, UAL Corp's United Airlines, Northwest Airlines Corp and America West Holdings Corp said they were now offering fares competitive with American's prices.
But both Delta Air Lines and USAir Group Inc said they had not made a decision yet on ticket fares.
American and its commuter carrier American Eagle announced a fare sale on Saturday with discounts of up to 50 percent on regular excursion fares.

The airline cut the fares only hours after President Bill Clinton stepped in to end a pilots' strike. He acted minutes after union leaders ordered all of American's 9,300 pilots to walk off the job at 12:01 a.m. Saturday (0501 GMT on Saturday).
The short-lived strike followed five days of intense negotiations with management which failed to bring agreement on a new four-year labor contract.
On Sunday, Continental spokeswoman Sarah Anthony said that: "We are competitive with American initiated in all the markets where they have dropped their fares."
Anthony said Continental lowered its fares on Saturday, as soon as it learned of the American reductions. Its sale is to end March 3, it said.

American's sales prices would apply to tickets bought between now and March 3 and no advance purchase was needed, the airline said. It was also offering double air miles and complimentary upgrades for its frequent flyers.
UAL Corp, parent of United Airlines, said it was matching American's cuts on both international and domestic flights, effective Sunday night.

American's discounts averaged 50 percent on excursion fares in all American and American Eagle markets in the United States, including Canada and Hawaii, for travel through March 14, with discounts of about 45 percent for travel until May 31. For European flights, fares would be up to 50 percent lower until May 31, the airline said.
Whitcomb said off-peak flights were Tuesday, Wednesday and Saturday, while special night flight rates were offered daily. They announced cuts effective Sunday.
A USAir spokesman said the airline was studying the issue but had not taken any action yet.
American pilots had threatened to strike over how much they were paid for flying big jets and whether or not union members should fly smaller jets for American Eagle.
American has said it needs to fly the small jets with lower-paid pilots from another union if it is to compete with other major carriers offering low-cost commuter flights.
When Clinton intervened on Saturday, he appointed a board to study the dispute and postponing a walkout for at least 60 days.
